subject: Private deployment throughput acceptance & egress thresholds

Subject: Private deployment throughput acceptance and network constraints

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As we move toward an onboarding window in June, Orion needs a concise acceptance checklist that ties throughput targets to the networking envelopes we'll commit to on our side. Procurement and infra will need specific numbers to include in their SOW.

High-level asks from Orion:
- Sustained inference target (tokens/s and QPS) for agreed model set (open-llama-70B variant)
- Warm-pool minutes and node counts required to meet 99th/95th latency targets
- Egress bandwidth per rack and recommended shaping to avoid bursts affecting other services
- Failure/fallback behavior when capacity is exceeded (e.g., degraded model, queued requests)

Would you be able to put together a short acceptance criteria doc and a one-sheet with the capacity headroom numbers? I've included Karthik and Naomi for ops details.

Also looping Samir from procurement (cc not included here) — they will want the contract addendum once we align on numbers.

Thanks,
Danielle

Subject: Re: Private deployment throughput acceptance and network constraints

Thanks Danielle — sending a proposed acceptance checklist and the capacity math below. Attaching runway_calc_v1.xlsx and a short egress profile PDF.

Summary (proposed for SOW):
- Target model mix: open-llama-70B-qlo (quantized baseline), ensemble reranker off by default
- Sustained throughput: 10,000 tokens/sec aggregate (approx. 220 QPS for 45-token average response)
- Sustained concurrency target: 200 concurrent inference requests (90s tail assumed per long jobs)
- Latency SLOs: 95th <= 120 ms (token generation), 99th <= 350 ms (end-to-end for short requests)
- GPU pool sizing (initial): 16x A100-equivalent (vCPU and NIC provisioning per node included)
- Warm pool: 4 reserved nodes (30% warm headroom) to keep KV cache hot — target warm pool hold time 20 minutes for active windows
- Admission control: queue depth cap 128, backpressure to fall back to smaller model or deny with 429-equivalent response when queue exceeds threshold
- Burst absorb window: 60s sustained burst at 1.5x baseline with autoscale triggers at 70% utilization
- Network: recommend 12 Gbps egress per rack (can be reduced to 8 Gbps with aggressive batching and prefix caching)
- Egress shaping: token-steady throttling + per-tenant caps; suggest policing at top-of-rack to avoid noisy-neighbor egress spikes
- Failover: automatic model fallback to 13B quantized variant + reroute to Dedicated pool in region as a secondary option

Operational notes:
- Warm pool sizing is conservative; if Orion enables aggressive KV cache sharing across requests we can reduce warm nodes.
- Quantization (8-bit) recommended for medium-latency workloads; we can provide runtime profiles.

Next steps I propose:
1) Karthik to validate admission control and network shaping knobs against your network ops constraints.
2) Naomi to sign off on observability hooks (trace/metrics) we must expose for SLO verification.
3) Once internal sign-off, we'll share a short addendum for Samir to attach to the SOW, then we'll initiate DocuSign.

Grace

On Tue, May 11, 2027 at 09:03, Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Summary (proposed for SOW):
> - Target model mix: open-llama-70B-qlo (quantized baseline), ensemble reranker off by default
> - Sustained throughput: 10,000 tokens/sec aggregate (approx. 220 QPS for 45-token average response)

Thanks Grace — good draft. A few operational clarifications and an alternate conservative scenario:

Operational clarifications:
- Warm pool: 4 nodes at A100 is fine for initial ramp, but to preserve KV cache hit-rate during heavy fanout we should consider 6 warm nodes (adds ~15% cost, reduces cold-start penalty).
- Cold-start recovery: recommend a churn policy that keeps nodes in warm pool for at least 20 minutes after last use; allow burst rehydration of up to 8 nodes for 10 minutes.
- Queue depth: 128 is reasonable; if Orion's front-end retries aggressively we should move to an adaptive admission queue with fast-fail thresholds at 200ms to prevent long tails.
- Egress: the 12 Gbps per rack recommendation assumes 50% of traffic is embeddings/auxiliary. If Orion's product is text-only with higher tokens/response, we need to budget +30% egress.

Conservative alternate (for contractual SLO buffer):
- Sustained throughput: plan for 13,000 tokens/sec (safety margin)
- GPU pool sizing (buffered): 20x A100-equivalent (allows sustained 1.3x throughput without spiking autoscale)
- Warm pool: 6 nodes (30s hold time)
- Autoscale policy: step-based scaling with immediate 30% burst capacity available via pre-warmed spare machines

I've added a second tab in the attached runway_calc_v1.xlsx with conservative numbers and a short egress_profile_v2.pdf showing shaping options. Mina — can you confirm the recommended NIC oversubscription and top-of-rack shaping knobs? Naomi — we'll need the tracing endpoints to verify the 95th/99th SLO during the acceptance window.

Karthik

- Baseline to include 20x A100-equivalent nodes, 6-node warm pool, 13k tokens/sec sustained target, admission queue cap 128 with adaptive fast-fail, and 12 Gbps egress per rack (we'll provision headroom for +30% if product confirms higher token density).

Procurement ask: please send a short addendum we can attach to the SOW with the bulletized acceptance criteria and the DocuSign link for signature. Samir — please confirm if you need further billing/legal terms.
